note: Hand-traced, deliberately simplified approximations of each kingdom's greatest extent. Ancient borders are uncertain and contested; see SOURCE.md.

kingdoms.name: Nanda Empire
kingdoms.summary: Magadha-based dynasty that first brought most of the Gangetic plain under one crown, famed in Greek and Indian sources for its wealth and vast army.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Dhana Nanda (c. 325 BCE)

cities.name: Pataliputra
cities.note: Nanda capital on the Ganges (modern Patna).

cities.name: Rajagriha
cities.note: Earlier capital of Magadha (modern Rajgir).

cities.name: Vaishali
cities.note: Old Licchavi city absorbed into Magadha.

cities.name: Kaushambi
cities.note: Former capital of the Vatsa kingdom on the Yamuna.

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Chief city of Avanti in Malwa.

events.title: Mahapadma Nanda's conquests
events.summary: Mahapadma Nanda overthrows the Shishunaga line and subdues the older kshatriya kingdoms; the Puranas call him the 'destroyer of all kshatriyas'.

events.title: Nanda rule reaches Kalinga
events.summary: The later Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela recalls a canal dug by a Nanda king, the key evidence for Nanda power in Kalinga.

events.title: Alexander halts at the Beas
events.summary: Alexander's exhausted army refuses to cross the Hyphasis (Beas); Greek writers cite reports of the huge Nanda army waiting beyond.

events.title: Fall of the Nandas
events.summary: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, overthrows Dhana Nanda and takes Pataliputra, founding the Maurya Empire.

kingdoms.name: Maurya Empire
kingdoms.summary: The first empire to unite most of the subcontinent, stretching from Afghanistan to Bengal and deep into the Deccan; under Ashoka it spread Buddhism and the dhamma edicts.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Ashoka (c. 250 BCE)

cities.name: Pataliputra
cities.note: Imperial capital; Megasthenes described its great timber walls.

cities.name: Taxila
cities.note: Seat of the north-western province and a famed centre of learning.

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Capital of the Avanti province; Ashoka served here as viceroy.

cities.name: Tosali
cities.note: Seat of the Kalinga province after the Kalinga War.

cities.name: Suvarnagiri
cities.note: Seat of the southern province, named in Ashoka's minor rock edicts.

cities.name: Sanchi
cities.note: Site of the Great Stupa, first commissioned by Ashoka.

cities.name: Sarnath
cities.note: Where Ashoka raised the Lion Capital, now India's national emblem.

events.title: Chandragupta founds the empire
events.summary: Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya overthrow the Nandas and make Pataliputra the imperial capital.

events.title: Seleucid–Mauryan war and treaty
events.summary: Seleucus I cedes Arachosia, Gedrosia and Paropamisadae in exchange for 500 war elephants, pushing the frontier into Afghanistan.

events.title: Megasthenes' embassy
events.summary: The Seleucid envoy Megasthenes lives at Pataliputra and writes the Indica, a key outside account of Mauryan India.

events.title: Chandragupta's final years
events.summary: Jain tradition holds that Chandragupta abdicated and ended his life by fasting (sallekhana) at Shravanabelagola.

events.title: Kalinga War
events.summary: Ashoka conquers Kalinga; the scale of death recorded in his edicts turns him toward Buddhism and rule by dhamma.

events.title: Major Rock Edicts
events.summary: Ashoka's edicts are carved across the empire, as at Girnar; they are among the oldest deciphered texts in India.

events.title: Kandahar bilingual inscription
events.summary: Ashoka addresses his far-western subjects in Greek and Aramaic, proof of the empire's reach into Afghanistan.

events.title: Third Buddhist Council
events.summary: Held at Pataliputra under Ashoka's patronage; missions are then sent to Sri Lanka, the Himalaya and beyond.

events.title: End of the Mauryas
events.summary: The general Pushyamitra Shunga assassinates the last Maurya emperor, Brihadratha, and founds the Shunga dynasty.

kingdoms.name: Pandya dynasty
kingdoms.summary: One of the three ancient Tamil crowns, ruling from Madurai for over 1,500 years; at its 13th-century peak it dominated the whole far south and northern Sri Lanka.

extents.label: Approximate extent at the 13th-century peak (c. 1270 CE)

cities.name: Madurai
cities.note: Pandya capital and seat of the legendary Tamil Sangams.

cities.name: Korkai
cities.note: Early Pandya port, famed for its pearl fisheries.

cities.name: Kayal
cities.note: Medieval Pandya port (modern Kayalpatnam) visited by Marco Polo.

cities.name: Tirunelveli
cities.note: Southern Pandya city on the Thamirabarani river.

events.title: Megasthenes hears of Pandaea
events.summary: The Greek envoy records a southern kingdom 'Pandaea', ruled by a queen and rich in pearls.

events.title: Named in Ashoka's edicts
events.summary: Ashoka's Rock Edict II lists the Pandyas among the independent kingdoms beyond his southern border.

events.title: Sangam literature
events.summary: Madurai's academies of poets produce the classical Tamil Sangam anthologies under Pandya patronage.

events.title: Kadungon revives the Pandyas
events.summary: Kadungon ends the Kalabhra interregnum and restores Pandya rule from Madurai.

events.title: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I
events.summary: The greatest Pandya conqueror subdues the Cholas, Hoysalas and Kakatiyas and levies tribute from Sri Lanka.

events.title: Marco Polo at Kayal
events.summary: The Venetian describes the wealth of the Pandya coast, its pearl trade and its horse imports.

events.title: Malik Kafur raids Madurai
events.summary: The Delhi Sultanate's general exploits a Pandya succession war and plunders the south.

events.title: Madurai Sultanate
events.summary: A sultanate seizes Madurai; Pandya princes survive only as local chiefs in the far south.

kingdoms.name: Indo-Greek Kingdom
kingdoms.summary: Hellenistic kings from Bactria who ruled the north-west; Menander debated Buddhism with the monk Nagasena, and their coins pioneered bilingual royal portraits.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Menander I (c. 150 BCE)

cities.name: Sagala
cities.note: Menander's capital (modern Sialkot).

cities.name: Taxila
cities.note: Old Gandharan city with an Indo-Greek quarter at Sirkap.

cities.name: Pushkalavati
cities.note: Ancient capital of Gandhara (modern Charsadda).

events.title: Demetrius crosses the Hindu Kush
events.summary: The Greco-Bactrian king Demetrius I invades Gandhara as Mauryan power fades.

events.title: Menander and Nagasena
events.summary: The Milindapanha records King Milinda (Menander) questioning the monk Nagasena on Buddhism.

events.title: Heliodorus pillar
events.summary: A Greek envoy from Taxila raises a pillar to Vasudeva (Krishna) at Vidisha, calling himself a devotee.

events.title: The last Indo-Greek kings
events.summary: Strato II's small eastern Punjab realm falls to the Indo-Scythians.

kingdoms.name: Satavahana dynasty
kingdoms.summary: The first great Deccan empire, ruling from Pratishthana and later Amaravati; patrons of both Vedic sacrifice and Buddhist monasteries, and controllers of the Roman sea trade.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Gautamiputra Satakarni (c. 125 CE)

cities.name: Pratishthana
cities.note: Western capital on the Godavari (modern Paithan).

cities.name: Dhanyakataka
cities.note: Later eastern capital beside the Amaravati stupa.

cities.name: Junnar
cities.note: Trade town ringed by Buddhist rock-cut caves.

cities.name: Nashik
cities.note: Site of the Pandavleni caves and royal inscriptions.

events.title: Naneghat inscription
events.summary: Queen Naganika records the Vedic sacrifices of Satakarni I on a mountain pass of the trade route to the coast.

events.title: Sanchi gateway gift
events.summary: An inscription credits a foreman of king Satakarni with carving on Sanchi's southern gateway.

events.title: Western Satraps defeated
events.summary: Gautamiputra Satakarni crushes Nahapana; his mother's Nashik inscription celebrates him as destroyer of the Shakas.

events.title: Rudradaman's Junagadh boast
events.summary: The Western Satrap claims on the Girnar rock to have twice defeated Satakarni, lord of the Deccan.

events.title: Amaravati stupa
events.summary: The great stupa is enlarged and faced with celebrated marble reliefs.

events.title: Yajna Sri Satakarni
events.summary: The last great Satavahana, whose ship-motif coins reflect the empire's sea trade.

events.title: Fragmentation
events.summary: The empire splinters among the Ikshvakus, Abhiras, Chutus and other successor states.

kingdoms.name: Kushan Empire
kingdoms.summary: Central Asian dynasty whose emperor Kanishka ruled from Bactria to the Ganges; its era produced Gandhara and Mathura art and carried Mahayana Buddhism along the Silk Road.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Kanishka (c. 130 CE)

cities.name: Purushapura
cities.note: Kanishka's capital (modern Peshawar).

cities.name: Mathura
cities.note: Southern capital and centre of Kushan sculpture.

cities.name: Kapisa
cities.note: Summer capital (modern Bagram).

cities.name: Taxila
cities.note: Gandharan city and monastery centre.

events.title: Kujula Kadphises unites the Kushans
events.summary: One of five Yuezhi clans absorbs the others and pushes into the Kabul valley and Gandhara.

events.title: Kanishka's reign
events.summary: The greatest Kushan emperor rules from Peshawar; his coins show Greek, Iranian and Indian gods including the Buddha.

events.title: Rabatak inscription
events.summary: A Bactrian-language inscription lists Kanishka's cities down to the Ganges plain.

events.title: Kanishka stupa
events.summary: A towering stupa at Peshawar, described by later Chinese pilgrims as the tallest in the world.

events.title: Fourth Buddhist Council
events.summary: Held in Kashmir under Kanishka's patronage, according to Sarvastivada tradition.

events.title: Gandhara and Mathura art
events.summary: Some of the first images of the Buddha in human form are carved in Gandhara and Mathura.

events.title: Sasanian conquest of Bactria
events.summary: Persian Sasanians take the western lands; later Kushans survive in the Punjab until the Gupta era.

kingdoms.name: Western Satraps
kingdoms.summary: Saka (Indo-Scythian) governors turned kings who ruled Gujarat and Malwa for nearly four centuries; Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is the earliest long Sanskrit inscription.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Rudradaman I (c. 150 CE)

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Capital of the Kardamaka line.

cities.name: Bharukaccha
cities.note: Great port the Greeks called Barygaza (modern Bharuch).

cities.name: Girinagara
cities.note: City below Girnar hill (modern Junagadh).

events.title: Barygaza in the Periplus
events.summary: A Greek sailing guide describes Barygaza's trade in wine, silver, spices and silk.

events.title: Chashtana at Ujjain
events.summary: The founder of the Kardamaka line rules from Ujjain; the Saka era of 78 CE may date from him.

events.title: Nahapana defeated
events.summary: The Kshaharata satrap loses his Deccan lands to Gautamiputra Satakarni.

events.title: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription
events.summary: Carved on the Ashokan rock at Girnar, it records the repair of the Sudarshana dam and Rudradaman's victories.

events.title: Gupta conquest
events.summary: Chandragupta II defeats Rudrasimha III and annexes Malwa and Gujarat.

kingdoms.name: Vakataka dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Deccan dynasty allied by marriage to the Guptas; under its last great king Harishena the finest paintings of the Ajanta caves were created.

extents.label: Approximate core territory (c. 450 CE)

cities.name: Nandivardhana
cities.note: Early capital of the main line (modern Nagardhan).

cities.name: Pravarapura
cities.note: Later capital founded by Pravarasena II (modern Mansar).

cities.name: Vatsagulma
cities.note: Seat of the Vatsagulma branch (modern Washim).

cities.name: Ajanta
cities.note: Buddhist cave monasteries in a river gorge.

events.title: Vatsagulma branch founded
events.summary: Sarvasena establishes a second Vakataka line at Vatsagulma.

events.title: Prabhavatigupta's regency
events.summary: The daughter of Gupta emperor Chandragupta II rules for her young sons after Rudrasena II's death.

events.title: Pravarasena II
events.summary: The king founds Pravarapura and is credited with the Prakrit epic Setubandha.

events.title: Ajanta's golden phase
events.summary: Under Harishena, courtiers sponsor most of Ajanta's later caves and their celebrated murals.

events.title: The Vakatakas fade
events.summary: After Harishena the dynasty vanishes from the record; work at Ajanta stops abruptly.

kingdoms.name: Pallava dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Kings of Kanchipuram whose rock-cut and structural temples at Mamallapuram laid the foundations of south Indian temple architecture.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Narasimhavarman I (c. 650 CE)

cities.name: Kanchipuram
cities.note: Pallava capital, 'the city of a thousand temples'.

cities.name: Mamallapuram
cities.note: Pallava port and showcase of their temple art.

events.title: First rock-cut temples
events.summary: Mahendravarman I boasts of a shrine made 'without brick, timber, metal or mortar'.

events.title: Xuanzang at Kanchi
events.summary: The Chinese pilgrim describes Kanchipuram as a great centre of Buddhist and Hindu learning.

events.title: Sack of Vatapi
events.summary: Narasimhavarman I avenges his father, kills Pulakeshin II and takes the title Vatapikonda.

events.title: Mamallapuram monuments
events.summary: The Pancha Rathas and the vast 'Descent of the Ganges' relief are carved from living rock.

events.title: Shore Temple
events.summary: Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) raises one of the earliest structural stone temples in the south.

events.title: Kailasanathar Temple
events.summary: Rajasimha's great Shiva temple at the capital, a model for later Dravidian temples.

events.title: Battle of Thiruppurambiyam
events.summary: Aparajita wins with Chola help, but the Cholas soon absorb the Pallava realm (c. 897).

kingdoms.name: Gupta Empire
kingdoms.summary: Often called a 'Golden Age': a north Indian empire whose era saw landmark advances in mathematics, astronomy, Sanskrit literature and temple art.

extents.label: Approximate directly ruled territory under Chandragupta II (c. 400 CE)

cities.name: Pataliputra
cities.note: Principal Gupta capital, as Faxian found it c. 400 CE.

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Western capital after Chandragupta II took Malwa.

cities.name: Prayaga
cities.note: Holy confluence city (modern Prayagraj).

cities.name: Mathura
cities.note: Great centre of Gupta-era sculpture.

cities.name: Vidisha
cities.note: Trade city beside the Udayagiri caves.

cities.name: Nalanda
cities.note: Buddhist university that drew scholars from across Asia.

events.title: Chandragupta I takes the throne
events.summary: Chandragupta I, strengthened by marriage into the Licchavis, takes the title maharajadhiraja; the Gupta era is reckoned from 319–320 CE.

events.title: Samudragupta's campaigns
events.summary: Harishena's praise-poem on the Allahabad Pillar records Samudragupta's conquests in the north and his southern expedition.

events.title: Conquest of the Western Satraps
events.summary: Chandragupta II ends Saka rule in Malwa and Gujarat, opening the western sea trade.

events.title: Faxian's pilgrimage
events.summary: The Chinese monk Faxian travels India (c. 399–412) and praises Pataliputra's hospitals and mild government.

events.title: Udayagiri caves
events.summary: Rock-cut shrines including the great Varaha panel, among the oldest surviving Hindu temple art.

events.title: Iron pillar
events.summary: A 7 m wrought-iron pillar, now at Mehrauli in Delhi, that has resisted rust for about 1,600 years.

events.title: Nalanda founded
events.summary: The Nalanda mahavihara is established, traditionally under Kumaragupta I, and grows into a great university.

events.title: Skandagupta repels the Hunas
events.summary: The Bhitari pillar inscription celebrates Skandagupta's victory over Huna invaders from Central Asia.

events.title: Aryabhata's Aryabhatiya
events.summary: Working at Kusumapura (Pataliputra), Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya on place-value arithmetic and astronomy.

events.title: Huna wars in Malwa
events.summary: The Eran inscription records Bhanugupta's battle as Alchon Hun raids break Gupta control of the west.

events.title: Gupta decline
events.summary: Weakened by the Huna wars and breakaway feudatories, the imperial line fades by the mid-6th century.

kingdoms.name: Alchon Huns
kingdoms.summary: Central Asian 'Huna' rulers who overran Gandhara and briefly much of north-western India, hastening the Gupta decline; Chinese pilgrims recorded Mihirakula's persecution of Buddhists.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Toramana and Mihirakula (c. 515 CE)

cities.name: Sakala
cities.note: Mihirakula's capital (modern Sialkot).

cities.name: Kapisa
cities.note: Alchon base in the Kabul valley, where their coins were struck.

cities.name: Eran
cities.note: Where a Toramana inscription marks the Huna advance into Malwa.

events.title: Gandhara overrun
events.summary: The Alchons take Gandhara; its Buddhist monasteries enter a long decline.

events.title: Toramana in Malwa
events.summary: The boar statue inscription at Eran is dated to Toramana's first regnal year.

events.title: Mihirakula's reign
events.summary: Remembered by Xuanzang and Kalhana as a cruel persecutor of Buddhists.

events.title: Song Yun meets the Hun king
events.summary: A Chinese envoy describes the warlike Hephthalite-era ruler of Gandhara.

events.title: Defeat by Yashodharman
events.summary: The Aulikara king Yashodharman defeats Mihirakula, commemorated by pillars at Sondani near Mandsaur.

events.title: Retreat to Kashmir
events.summary: Driven out of the plains, Mihirakula is said to have seized Kashmir.

kingdoms.name: Chalukyas of Badami
kingdoms.summary: Deccan dynasty from Vatapi (Badami) whose temples at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal blend northern and southern styles; the later Western and Eastern Chalukyas are offshoots.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Pulakeshin II (c. 640 CE)

cities.name: Vatapi
cities.note: Cliff-ringed capital with cave temples (modern Badami).

cities.name: Aihole
cities.note: Early temple town, a 'cradle' of Indian temple architecture.

cities.name: Pattadakal
cities.note: Coronation town with a UNESCO-listed temple group.

cities.name: Vengi
cities.note: Seat of the Eastern Chalukya branch.

events.title: Vatapi fortified
events.summary: Pulakeshin I fortifies the hill of Vatapi and performs the horse sacrifice, founding the dynasty.

events.title: Harsha halted on the Narmada
events.summary: Pulakeshin II defeats Harsha somewhere on the Narmada, capping northern expansion (marker indicative).

events.title: Eastern Chalukyas at Vengi
events.summary: Pulakeshin's brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana rules the conquered east coast, founding a line that lasts 400 years.

events.title: Aihole inscription
events.summary: Court poet Ravikirti's Sanskrit eulogy of Pulakeshin II on the Meguti temple.

events.title: Vatapi sacked by the Pallavas
events.summary: Narasimhavarman I kills Pulakeshin II and holds the capital for over a decade.

events.title: Kanchi taken
events.summary: Vikramaditya II captures the Pallava capital but, unusually, spares and endows its temples.

events.title: Virupaksha Temple
events.summary: Queen Lokamahadevi builds Pattadakal's grandest temple to commemorate the victory.

events.title: Overthrown by Dantidurga
events.summary: The Rashtrakuta feudatory Dantidurga defeats Kirtivarman II and takes over the Deccan.

kingdoms.name: Harsha's empire
kingdoms.summary: Harshavardhana of the Pushyabhuti dynasty reunited much of north India from Kannauj; a patron of Buddhism and Shaivism and himself a playwright.

extents.label: Approximate extent of Harsha's authority (c. 640 CE)

cities.name: Kanyakubja
cities.note: Harsha's imperial capital (modern Kannauj).

cities.name: Sthanvishvara
cities.note: Ancestral Pushyabhuti capital (modern Thanesar).

cities.name: Prayaga
cities.note: Holy confluence where Harsha gave away his treasury.

cities.name: Nalanda
cities.note: Great Buddhist university that Harsha endowed.

events.title: Harsha takes the throne
events.summary: After his brother's murder, the sixteen-year-old Harsha becomes king of Thanesar; his life is told in Banabhatta's Harshacharita.

events.title: Defeat on the Narmada
events.summary: Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas blocks Harsha's march into the Deccan (marker indicative).

events.title: Embassy to Tang China
events.summary: Harsha opens diplomatic relations with Emperor Taizong; Chinese envoys return the visit.

events.title: Kannauj assembly
events.summary: Harsha convenes a great religious assembly at which Xuanzang expounds Mahayana doctrine.

events.title: Prayaga almsgiving
events.summary: At the quinquennial assembly Harsha distributes his wealth, down to his own robes, as Xuanzang records.

events.title: Death of Harsha
events.summary: Harsha dies without an heir and his empire quickly breaks apart.

kingdoms.name: Karkota dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Kashmiri dynasty known chiefly from Kalhana's Rajatarangini; under Lalitaditya Muktapida it briefly projected power across north India.

extents.label: Approximate core territory (Kashmir and its hills)

cities.name: Pravarapura
cities.note: Kashmir's capital (modern Srinagar).

cities.name: Parihasapura
cities.note: Lalitaditya's new capital, now ruins.

events.title: Xuanzang in Kashmir
events.summary: The pilgrim spends two years studying in Kashmir under Durlabhavardhana's rule.

events.title: Lalitaditya defeats Kannauj
events.summary: Lalitaditya Muktapida defeats Yashovarman of Kannauj; the Rajatarangini credits him with vast campaigns.

events.title: Parihasapura founded
events.summary: Lalitaditya builds a new capital with a colossal Buddhist stupa and Vishnu temples.

events.title: Martand Sun Temple
events.summary: Lalitaditya raises a monumental sun temple on a plateau above the Kashmir valley.

events.title: Utpala dynasty
events.summary: Avantivarman founds the Utpala dynasty and the temple town of Avantipura.

kingdoms.name: Arab rule in Sindh
kingdoms.summary: The Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711–712; Arab emirates at Mansura and Multan followed until the Ghaznavid conquest.

extents.label: Approximate extent (Sindh and Multan, c. 720 CE)

cities.name: Mansura
cities.note: Arab capital of Sindh, near old Brahmanabad.

cities.name: Multan
cities.note: Seat of the Emirate of Multan.

cities.name: Debal
cities.note: Indus-delta port where the conquest began (modern Banbhore).

cities.name: Aror
cities.note: Capital of Raja Dahir's kingdom.

events.title: Debal falls
events.summary: Muhammad bin Qasim storms the port after a siege with catapults.

events.title: Death of Raja Dahir
events.summary: The last Hindu king of Sindh is killed in battle and his kingdom annexed to the Caliphate.

events.title: Multan taken
events.summary: The conquest reaches the sun-temple city of Multan in southern Punjab.

events.title: Habbari emirate
events.summary: An Arab family makes Sindh a hereditary, practically independent emirate from Mansura.

events.title: Ismaili Multan
events.summary: Multan becomes an Ismaili state allied to the Fatimids of Egypt.

events.title: Ghaznavid conquest
events.summary: Mahmud of Ghazni subdues Multan and Mansura, ending the Arab emirates.

kingdoms.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Rulers of Kannauj who held back Arab expansion east of the Indus and fought the Palas and Rashtrakutas for north India in the Tripartite Struggle.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Mihira Bhoja (c. 870 CE)

cities.name: Kannauj
cities.note: Imperial capital from Nagabhata II onward.

cities.name: Bhinmal
cities.note: Early Gurjara centre in southern Rajasthan.

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Early Pratihara base in Malwa.

cities.name: Gopadri
cities.note: Hill fortress (modern Gwalior) with Pratihara-era temples.

events.title: Arab invasions repulsed
events.summary: Nagabhata I and allied kings turn back Umayyad raiders, halting Arab expansion beyond Sindh.

events.title: Osian temples
events.summary: A desert trade town fills with early Maru-Gurjara temples to Vishnu, Surya, Harihara and the Jain Mahavira.

events.title: Nagabhata II takes Kannauj
events.summary: Nagabhata II defeats the Pala-backed ruler and makes Kannauj his capital.

events.title: Mihira Bhoja's reign
events.summary: Over nearly fifty years Mihira Bhoja builds the dynasty's greatest empire.

events.title: Kannauj sacked by Indra III
events.summary: The Rashtrakuta king briefly takes the capital, a blow from which Pratihara power never fully recovers.

events.title: Mahmud of Ghazni at Kannauj
events.summary: Mahmud sacks the capital; the weakened dynasty ends within two decades.

kingdoms.name: Pala Empire
kingdoms.summary: A Buddhist dynasty of Bengal and Bihar (not Hindu), patrons of Nalanda and Vikramashila, whose scholars carried Buddhism to Tibet.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Devapala (c. 850 CE)

cities.name: Mudgagiri
cities.note: Royal camp-capital on the Ganges (modern Munger).

cities.name: Pataliputra
cities.note: Old imperial city, still a Pala seat.

cities.name: Gauda
cities.note: Heartland of Bengal, which gave its name to the region.

cities.name: Vikramashila
cities.note: Pala-founded Buddhist university.

cities.name: Nalanda
cities.note: Ancient university richly endowed by the Palas.

events.title: Gopala chosen king
events.summary: Tradition says Bengal's chiefs elected Gopala to end a period of anarchy ('matsyanyaya').

events.title: Dharmapala at Kannauj
events.summary: Dharmapala installs his own nominee on the throne of Kannauj in the Tripartite Struggle.

events.title: Somapura Mahavihara
events.summary: Dharmapala builds one of the largest Buddhist monasteries south of the Himalaya.

events.title: Vikramashila founded
events.summary: Dharmapala founds a second great university, a centre of tantric Buddhism.

events.title: Devapala's Nalanda grant
events.summary: A copper plate records villages granted to a monastery built at Nalanda by the king of Srivijaya.

events.title: Atisha goes to Tibet
events.summary: The Vikramashila master Atisha travels to Tibet and reshapes Tibetan Buddhism.

events.title: Varendra rebellion
events.summary: Kaivarta chiefs seize northern Bengal until Ramapala wins it back.

events.title: The Senas take over
events.summary: The Hindu Sena dynasty displaces the last Palas in Bengal.

kingdoms.name: Rashtrakuta dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Deccan emperors from Manyakheta who raided as far as the Ganges and Kanchi; an Arab visitor counted their king among the four great sovereigns of the world.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I (c. 800–820 CE)

cities.name: Manyakheta
cities.note: Imperial capital from Amoghavarsha I (modern Malkhed).

cities.name: Elapura
cities.note: Rock-cut cave complex (modern Ellora).

cities.name: Lattalura
cities.note: Ancestral home of the dynasty (modern Latur).

events.title: Dantidurga's rise
events.summary: Dantidurga overthrows his Chalukya overlords; his inscription survives in Ellora's Dashavatara cave.

events.title: Kailasa temple
events.summary: Krishna I has a whole temple carved downward out of a single basalt hillside.

events.title: Rashtrakutas on the Ganges
events.summary: Dhruva and Govinda III defeat both Pratiharas and Palas in the Doab during the Tripartite Struggle.

events.title: Manyakheta built
events.summary: Amoghavarsha I founds a new capital, 'a city to shame the city of the gods'.

events.title: Kavirajamarga
events.summary: The earliest surviving work of Kannada literature, a treatise on poetics, is written at Amoghavarsha's court.

events.title: Battle of Takkolam
events.summary: Krishna III crushes the Cholas and occupies their northern lands.

events.title: Manyakheta sacked
events.summary: The Paramara king Siyaka plunders the capital, exposing Rashtrakuta weakness.

events.title: End of the Rashtrakutas
events.summary: Tailapa II restores Chalukya rule; the last Rashtrakuta claimant dies soon after.

kingdoms.name: Paramara dynasty (Raja Bhoja)
kingdoms.summary: Rulers of Malwa from Dhara, famous above all for Raja Bhoja (c. 1010–1055), a warrior, builder and polymath credited with dozens of Sanskrit treatises.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Bhoja (c. 1040 CE)

cities.name: Dhara
cities.note: Bhoja's capital and centre of learning (modern Dhar).

cities.name: Ujjayini
cities.note: Earlier Paramara capital.

cities.name: Mandapa-Durga
cities.note: Hill fortress (modern Mandu).

cities.name: Chitrakuta
cities.note: Fortress held by Bhoja (modern Chittorgarh).

events.title: Siyaka sacks Manyakheta
events.summary: Throwing off Rashtrakuta overlordship, Siyaka plunders their capital and makes Malwa independent.

events.title: Munja's defeat
events.summary: The poet-king Vakpati Munja is captured and killed by the Chalukya Tailapa II after a failed invasion.

events.title: Raja Bhoja's reign begins
events.summary: Bhoja rules for some 45 years, fighting on every frontier and becoming a legend of the ideal king.

events.title: Bhoja the scholar
events.summary: Works on architecture (Samarangana Sutradhara), poetics and yoga are attributed to him; he founds a Sanskrit college at Dhara.

events.title: Bhojeshwar Temple
events.summary: An unfinished Shiva temple at Bhojpur with one of India's largest lingas and its original building plans engraved nearby.

events.title: Death of Bhoja
events.summary: Bhoja dies as the Chaulukya and Kalachuri kings jointly invade Malwa.

events.title: Conquest by Alauddin Khalji
events.summary: The Delhi Sultanate conquers Malwa and ends Paramara rule.

kingdoms.name: Hindu Shahi dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Brahmin-led kingdom of the Kabul valley, Gandhara and Punjab that for two centuries guarded the north-west passes before falling to the Ghaznavids.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 950 CE)

cities.name: Kabul
cities.note: First Shahi capital.

cities.name: Udabhandapura
cities.note: Later capital on the Indus (modern Hund).

cities.name: Lahore
cities.note: Eastern Shahi city in Punjab.

cities.name: Nandana
cities.note: Salt Range fortress, the last Shahi stronghold.

events.title: Kallar founds the dynasty
events.summary: The Brahmin minister Kallar displaces the last Turk Shahi ruler of Kabul.

events.title: Capital moves to the Indus
events.summary: As the Saffarids take Kabul, the Shahis rule from Udabhandapura.

events.title: Salt Range temples
events.summary: Tall Kashmiri-style temples such as those at Amb are built across the Shahi Salt Range.

events.title: Battle of Peshawar
events.summary: Mahmud of Ghazni defeats and captures Jayapala, who later ends his own life.

events.title: Defeat at Chach
events.summary: Anandapala's coalition army is routed by Mahmud on the Chach plain.

events.title: Fall of Nandana
events.summary: Mahmud storms the Salt Range fortress held by Trilochanapala's son.

events.title: End of the Shahis
events.summary: The last king, Bhimapala, dies and the dynasty is extinguished.

kingdoms.name: Chola Empire (imperial Cholas)
kingdoms.summary: Tamil maritime empire whose fleets reached Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Southeast Asia, and whose bronzes and temples are high points of Indian art.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Rajendra I (c. 1030 CE)

cities.name: Thanjavur
cities.note: Capital of Vijayalaya and Rajaraja I.

cities.name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram
cities.note: Rajendra I's new capital, 'city of the Chola who took the Ganges'.

cities.name: Kanchipuram
cities.note: Former Pallava capital, a major Chola city.

cities.name: Nagapattinam
cities.note: Chief port for the Southeast Asia trade.

cities.name: Polonnaruwa
cities.note: Chola seat in Sri Lanka, renamed Jananathapuram.

events.title: Vijayalaya takes Thanjavur
events.summary: A Pallava feudatory seizes Thanjavur and revives the ancient Chola name.

events.title: Conquest of Anuradhapura
events.summary: Rajaraja I invades Sri Lanka, sacks the old capital and annexes the north.

events.title: Brihadisvara Temple
events.summary: Rajaraja I completes the colossal granite temple at Thanjavur, crowned by an 80-ton capstone.

events.title: Expedition to the Ganges
events.summary: Rajendra I's army reaches Bengal; Ganges water is carried home to sanctify his new capital.

events.title: Raid on Srivijaya
events.summary: A Chola fleet sacks Kadaram (Kedah) and other ports of the Srivijaya empire.

events.title: Kulothunga I unites the crowns
events.summary: An Eastern Chalukya prince takes the Chola throne, joining Vengi to the empire.

events.title: End of the Cholas
events.summary: The resurgent Pandyas defeat Rajendra III, the last Chola king.

kingdoms.name: Ghaznavid Empire
kingdoms.summary: Turkic dynasty from Ghazni; Mahmud's seventeen raids plundered north India's temple cities, and the dynasty later ruled Punjab from Lahore.

extents.label: Approximate eastern extent under Mahmud (c. 1030 CE; Khorasan and Iran omitted)

cities.name: Ghazni
cities.note: Dynastic capital, enriched with Indian plunder.

cities.name: Lahore
cities.note: Eastern capital and, from c. 1163, the last one.

cities.name: Peshawar
cities.note: Gateway city below the Khyber Pass.

cities.name: Multan
cities.note: Southern Punjab city taken in 1010.

events.title: Sabuktigin founds the dynasty
events.summary: A former slave commander takes Ghazni and begins raiding the Hindu Shahis.

events.title: Battle of Peshawar
events.summary: Mahmud defeats the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala.

events.title: Mathura and Kannauj sacked
events.summary: Mahmud's deepest raid plunders the temple city of Mathura and the Pratihara capital.

events.title: Raid on Somnath
events.summary: Mahmud sacks the Somnath temple on the Gujarat coast, a raid long remembered in Indian memory.

events.title: Al-Biruni's India
events.summary: The scholar Al-Biruni, who travelled with Mahmud, completes his careful study of Indian science and religion.

events.title: Retreat to Lahore
events.summary: Losing Ghazni to the Ghurids, the dynasty is left with the Punjab.

events.title: Lahore falls to the Ghurids
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghor captures the last Ghaznavid sultan, Khusrau Malik.

kingdoms.name: Hoysala Empire
kingdoms.summary: Karnataka dynasty celebrated for star-shaped temples covered in intricate soapstone carving at Belur, Halebidu and Somanathapura.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 1250 CE)

cities.name: Dwarasamudra
cities.note: Hoysala capital (modern Halebidu).

cities.name: Belur
cities.note: Early capital on the Yagachi river.

cities.name: Kannanur
cities.note: Southern capital near Srirangam.

cities.name: Tiruvannamalai
cities.note: Last seat of Veera Ballala III.

events.title: Victory at Talakad
events.summary: Vishnuvardhana drives the Cholas out of Gangavadi and becomes an independent power.

events.title: Chennakeshava Temple
events.summary: Vishnuvardhana's temple at Belur, carved over 103 years, celebrates the Talakad victory.

events.title: Hoysaleswara Temple
events.summary: The twin Shiva temple at the capital, with friezes of elephants, lions and epics.

events.title: Somanathapura
events.summary: The general Somanatha builds the Chennakesava temple, the last great Hoysala shrine.

events.title: Malik Kafur takes the capital
events.summary: Veera Ballala III submits to the Delhi Sultanate's army and Dwarasamudra is plundered.

events.title: Death of Veera Ballala III
events.summary: The last major Hoysala king is killed fighting the Madurai Sultanate.

kingdoms.name: Eastern Ganga dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Kings of Kalinga (Odisha) who built the Jagannath temple at Puri and the Sun Temple at Konark.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 1250 CE)

cities.name: Kataka
cities.note: Capital 'Abhinava Varanasi Kataka' (modern Cuttack).

cities.name: Kalinganagara
cities.note: Early capital (modern Mukhalingam).

cities.name: Puri
cities.note: Temple city of Jagannath.

cities.name: Konark
cities.note: Coastal site of the Sun Temple.

events.title: Anantavarman Chodaganga
events.summary: The king begins a 70-year reign uniting Kalinga from the Ganges delta to the Godavari.

events.title: Jagannath Temple
events.summary: Chodaganga begins the present temple at Puri, one of Hinduism's great pilgrimage centres.

events.title: Capital at Cuttack
events.summary: Anangabhima III rules from Cuttack and dedicates his kingdom to Jagannath.

events.title: Konark Sun Temple
events.summary: Narasimhadeva I builds the Sun god's temple as a colossal stone chariot with 24 carved wheels.

events.title: The Gajapatis take over
events.summary: Kapilendra Deva seizes the throne and founds the Gajapati empire.

kingdoms.name: Kakatiya dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Telugu dynasty from Warangal that united the Andhra country, built great irrigation tanks, and was ruled for a generation by the queen Rudrama Devi.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 1290 CE)

cities.name: Orugallu
cities.note: Fortified capital (modern Warangal).

cities.name: Hanamkonda
cities.note: Early capital beside Warangal.

cities.name: Motupalli
cities.note: Chief seaport of the kingdom.

events.title: Independence and the Thousand Pillar Temple
events.summary: Rudradeva throws off Chalukya overlordship and dedicates the Thousand Pillar Temple.

events.title: Ramappa Temple
events.summary: General Recherla Rudra builds a temple of 'floating' lightweight bricks, now a UNESCO site.

events.title: Rudrama Devi rules
events.summary: One of the few ruling queens of medieval India holds the kingdom against rebels and rivals.

events.title: Marco Polo at Motupalli
events.summary: The Venetian praises the kingdom's diamonds, fine cloth and just queen.

events.title: Siege of Warangal
events.summary: Prataparudra buys peace from Malik Kafur with an enormous tribute.

events.title: Fall of Warangal
events.summary: Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughluq) captures the city and ends the dynasty.

kingdoms.name: Ghurid dynasty
kingdoms.summary: Dynasty from the mountains of Ghur whose ruler Muhammad of Ghor defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at Tarain (1192), laying the foundation of Turkic rule in north India.

extents.label: Approximate extent at Muhammad of Ghor's death (1206 CE)

cities.name: Firozkoh
cities.note: Mountain capital in Ghur, marked by the Minaret of Jam.

cities.name: Ghazni
cities.note: Seat of Muhammad of Ghor.

cities.name: Lahore
cities.note: Taken from the Ghaznavids in 1186.

cities.name: Delhi
cities.note: Chauhan fort taken after Tarain, seat of Qutb ud-Din Aibak.

events.title: Multan taken
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghor begins his Indian campaigns by seizing Multan from its Ismaili rulers.

events.title: Defeat at Kasahrada
events.summary: The Chaulukya army of Gujarat routs the Ghurids near Mount Abu.

events.title: First Battle of Tarain
events.summary: Prithviraj Chauhan defeats Muhammad of Ghor, who is wounded and retreats.

events.title: Second Battle of Tarain
events.summary: Muhammad returns and defeats Prithviraj; Delhi and Ajmer fall.

events.title: Battle of Chandawar
events.summary: Jayachandra of Kannauj is killed and the Gangetic plain opens to Ghurid armies.

events.title: Qutb Minar begun
events.summary: Qutb ud-Din Aibak starts the great minaret beside Delhi's first congregational mosque.

events.title: Bakhtiyar Khalji in Bihar and Bengal
events.summary: His raids sack the monastery of Odantapuri and take Nadia; the great Buddhist universities decline soon after.

events.title: Muhammad of Ghor killed
events.summary: He is assassinated at Damyak on the Jhelum; his generals found the Delhi Sultanate.

kingdoms.name: Mamluk dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)
kingdoms.summary: The first Delhi Sultanate dynasty, founded by Muhammad of Ghor's slave-general Qutb ud-Din Aibak; Iltutmish and Razia consolidated it and Balban held off the Mongols.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Iltutmish (c. 1236 CE)

cities.name: Delhi
cities.note: Capital around the Qutb complex at Mehrauli.

cities.name: Lahore
cities.note: Where Aibak was crowned.

cities.name: Badaun
cities.note: Iltutmish's governorship before he became sultan.

cities.name: Lakhnauti
cities.note: Seat of the Bengal governors (Gaur).

events.title: Qutb ud-Din Aibak crowned
events.summary: Muhammad of Ghor's former slave becomes the first sultan of Delhi.

events.title: Iltutmish
events.summary: Aibak's son-in-law makes Delhi the capital and wins recognition from the Abbasid caliph.

events.title: Genghis Khan at the Indus
events.summary: Iltutmish refuses asylum to the fleeing Khwarazm prince, keeping the Mongols out of India.

events.title: Qutb Minar completed
events.summary: Iltutmish adds the upper storeys to Aibak's minaret.

events.title: Razia Sultana
events.summary: The only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate holds power for nearly four years.

events.title: Balban
events.summary: A stern, ceremonious sultan who crushes rebels and fortifies the frontier against the Mongols.

events.title: The Khaljis take over
events.summary: Jalal-ud-din Khalji deposes the last, infant Mamluk sultan.

kingdoms.name: Khalji dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)
kingdoms.summary: Alauddin Khalji repelled repeated Mongol invasions, imposed market price controls, and sent Malik Kafur's armies deep into the south.

extents.label: Approximate directly ruled territory under Alauddin (c. 1311 CE; southern kingdoms paid tribute)

cities.name: Delhi
cities.note: Alauddin's new fort of Siri.

cities.name: Devagiri
cities.note: Yadava capital made a Khalji vassal.

cities.name: Anhilwara
cities.note: Old Gujarat capital (modern Patan).

events.title: Jalal-ud-din Khalji
events.summary: An elderly Khalji noble founds the dynasty.

events.title: Alauddin seizes the throne
events.summary: Returning rich from a raid on Devagiri, Alauddin murders his uncle and becomes sultan.

events.title: Conquest of Gujarat
events.summary: Khalji generals take Gujarat, also looting Somnath once more.

events.title: Siege of Chittor
events.summary: Alauddin takes the Guhila fortress, an episode later retold in the legend of Padmavati.

events.title: Conquest of Malwa
events.summary: The Paramara kingdom falls to Khalji armies.

events.title: Alai Darwaza
events.summary: A domed gateway at the Qutb complex, the first building in India built with true arches and dome.

events.title: Malik Kafur reaches Madurai
events.summary: The general's southern campaign plunders the Hoysala and Pandya capitals.

events.title: The Tughlaqs take over
events.summary: Ghazi Malik (Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq) overthrows the usurper Khusrau Khan.

kingdoms.name: Tughlaq dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)
kingdoms.summary: Under Muhammad bin Tughluq the Delhi Sultanate reached almost the whole subcontinent, before revolts, the ill-fated move to Daulatabad and Timur's sack of Delhi broke it up.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Muhammad bin Tughluq (c. 1335 CE)

cities.name: Tughlaqabad
cities.note: Ghiyath al-Din's massive fortress-city at Delhi.

cities.name: Daulatabad
cities.note: Second capital, formerly Devagiri.

cities.name: Jaunpur
cities.note: Founded by Firuz Shah in 1359.

cities.name: Madurai
cities.note: Southernmost province (Ma'bar) until its revolt in 1335.

events.title: Tughlaqabad built
events.summary: Ghiyath al-Din raises a vast fortified capital in four years.

events.title: Muhammad bin Tughluq
events.summary: A brilliant but erratic sultan, known for token copper currency and grand schemes.

events.title: Capital moved to Daulatabad
events.summary: Delhi's population is ordered south to the Deccan; the move is soon reversed.

events.title: Ibn Battuta in Delhi
events.summary: The Moroccan traveller serves as a judge at the sultan's court for several years.

events.title: The Deccan breaks away
events.summary: Rebel nobles found the Bahmani Sultanate, following the earlier loss of Madurai and the rise of Vijayanagara.

events.title: Firuz Shah Tughlaq
events.summary: A long, milder reign of canals, new towns and the re-erection of two Ashokan pillars at Delhi.

events.title: Timur sacks Delhi
events.summary: The Central Asian conqueror massacres much of Delhi's population and carries off its artisans.

events.title: The Sayyids take over
events.summary: Timur's former governor Khizr Khan occupies Delhi.

kingdoms.name: Vijayanagara Empire
kingdoms.summary: The last great Hindu empire of the south; its capital at Hampi was among the largest and richest cities of the 16th-century world.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Krishnadevaraya (c. 1520 CE)

cities.name: Vijayanagara
cities.note: The 'City of Victory' on the Tungabhadra (modern Hampi).

cities.name: Penukonda
cities.note: Capital after the fall of Hampi.

cities.name: Chandragiri
cities.note: Late capital with its royal palace.

cities.name: Madurai
cities.note: Seat of the Nayak governors.

events.title: Harihara and Bukka found the empire
events.summary: The Sangama brothers found a new capital on the Tungabhadra.

events.title: Madurai Sultanate ended
events.summary: Prince Kumara Kampana conquers Madurai, a campaign sung by his queen Gangadevi in the Madhura Vijayam.

events.title: Abdur Razzaq's embassy
events.summary: The Persian envoy writes that the eye had never seen a place like Vijayanagara.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya crowned
events.summary: The empire's greatest king, a warrior and Telugu poet, begins a 20-year golden age.

events.title: Battle of Raichur
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya defeats the Bijapur Sultanate and takes the Raichur doab.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: The Deccan Sultanates defeat Rama Raya; Hampi is sacked and abandoned.

events.title: End of the empire
events.summary: Sriranga III, the last emperor, loses his remaining lands around Vellore to the Deccan Sultanates.

kingdoms.name: Bahmani Sultanate
kingdoms.summary: The first independent sultanate of the Deccan, founded in revolt against Muhammad bin Tughluq; it fought Vijayanagara for a century and then split into five Deccan sultanates.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Mahmud Gawan (c. 1475 CE)

cities.name: Gulbarga
cities.note: First Bahmani capital (Ahsanabad).

cities.name: Bidar
cities.note: Capital from c. 1429.

cities.name: Daulatabad
cities.note: Hill fortress where the revolt began.

events.title: Bahman Shah founds the sultanate
events.summary: Rebel Deccan nobles crown Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah at Gulbarga.

events.title: Gulbarga's great mosque
events.summary: A mosque roofed entirely with domes rises inside the Gulbarga fort.

events.title: Capital moves to Bidar
events.summary: Ahmad Shah I rebuilds Bidar fort as his new capital.

events.title: Afanasy Nikitin at Bidar
events.summary: A Russian merchant records life in the Bahmani capital.

events.title: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa
events.summary: The chief minister founds a great Persian-style college with tiled minarets.

events.title: Execution of Mahmud Gawan
events.summary: Court intrigue brings down the minister, and the sultanate starts to fragment.

events.title: Five successor sultanates
events.summary: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Berar and Bidar go their own ways.

kingdoms.name: Bengal Sultanate
kingdoms.summary: Independent sultanate that united Bengal, rich from textiles and trade; it patronised Bengali literature and built distinctive brick and terracotta mosques.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Alauddin Husain Shah (c. 1500 CE)

cities.name: Pandua
cities.note: Early capital with the Adina Mosque.

cities.name: Gaur
cities.note: Later capital and one of the largest cities of its age.

cities.name: Sonargaon
cities.note: Eastern capital and textile centre.

cities.name: Chittagong
cities.note: Main seaport.

events.title: Ilyas Shah unites Bengal
events.summary: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah joins Bengal's three regions into one sultanate.

events.title: Adina Mosque
events.summary: Sikandar Shah builds what was then the largest mosque in the subcontinent.

events.title: Ming treasure fleet
events.summary: Zheng He's voyages bring Chinese envoys, and Bengal sends a giraffe to the Ming court.

events.title: Raja Ganesha
events.summary: A Hindu noble seizes power; his son converts and rules as Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah.

events.title: Alauddin Husain Shah
events.summary: A golden age of Bengali literature and the Chaitanya bhakti movement flourishes under his rule.

events.title: Sher Shah takes Gaur
events.summary: The Afghan Sher Khan captures the capital, the start of the Sur Empire.

events.title: Battle of Rajmahal
events.summary: Akbar's army defeats Daud Khan Karrani and annexes Bengal.

kingdoms.name: Malwa Sultanate
kingdoms.summary: Central Indian sultanate ruled from the hill-fortress of Mandu, whose palaces and the romance of Baz Bahadur and Rupmati survive.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 1470 CE)

cities.name: Mandu
cities.note: Capital on a fortified plateau, 'Shadiabad', the city of joy.

cities.name: Dhar
cities.note: Former Paramara capital, the first sultans' seat.

cities.name: Chanderi
cities.note: Fortress town famed for its fine textiles.

events.title: Dilawar Khan breaks away
events.summary: The Tughlaq governor of Malwa becomes independent as Delhi weakens.

events.title: Capital moves to Mandu
events.summary: Hoshang Shah makes the plateau fortress his capital.

events.title: Hoshang Shah's Tomb
events.summary: India's earliest monument built entirely of marble, said to have inspired the Taj Mahal's builders.

events.title: Jahaz Mahal
events.summary: Ghiyath Shah's 'ship palace' between two lakes, built for his vast harem.

events.title: Conquered by Gujarat
events.summary: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat takes Mandu; Malwa changes hands several times after.

events.title: Baz Bahadur defeated
events.summary: Akbar's general defeats the musician-king at Sarangpur; Rupmati takes her own life rather than be captured.

kingdoms.name: Gujarat Sultanate
kingdoms.summary: Wealthy maritime sultanate founded by Muzaffar Shah; Ahmedabad's mosques blend Islamic forms with Gujarati temple craftsmanship.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Mahmud Begada (c. 1500 CE)

cities.name: Ahmedabad
cities.note: Capital founded by Ahmad Shah I in 1411.

cities.name: Champaner
cities.note: Mahmud Begada's capital, now a UNESCO site.

cities.name: Cambay
cities.note: Great port on the gulf (modern Khambhat).

cities.name: Diu
cities.note: Island port, lost to the Portuguese in 1535.

events.title: Muzaffar Shah I
events.summary: The Tughlaq governor declares Gujarat independent.

events.title: Ahmedabad founded
events.summary: Ahmad Shah I builds a new capital on the Sabarmati.

events.title: Champaner taken
events.summary: Mahmud Begada captures the hill fort of Pavagadh and builds a new capital below it.

events.title: Battle of Diu
events.summary: A Portuguese fleet defeats the allied Gujarati, Mamluk and Calicut navies, winning control of Indian Ocean trade.

events.title: Death of Bahadur Shah
events.summary: The sultan drowns in a clash with the Portuguese at Diu.

events.title: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque and annexation
events.summary: The famous tree-of-life stone lattice is carved as Akbar annexes Gujarat.

kingdoms.name: Sayyid dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)
kingdoms.summary: Founded by Timur's governor Khizr Khan, the Sayyids ruled a much-reduced Delhi Sultanate around Delhi and eastern Punjab.

extents.label: Approximate extent (c. 1420 CE)

cities.name: Delhi
cities.note: A shrunken capital after Timur's sack.

cities.name: Sirhind
cities.note: Key fortress on the Punjab road.

events.title: Khizr Khan takes Delhi
events.summary: He rules as Timur's deputy rather than taking the title of sultan.

events.title: Mubarak Shah
events.summary: Khizr's son claims full sovereignty and fights constant revolts.

events.title: Tomb of Muhammad Shah
events.summary: An octagonal tomb, now in Delhi's Lodhi Gardens, sets a model for later Delhi tombs.

events.title: Abdication to the Lodis
events.summary: Alam Shah retires to Badaun and hands Delhi to Bahlul Lodi.

kingdoms.name: Lodi dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)
kingdoms.summary: Afghan dynasty that revived the Delhi Sultanate; Sikandar Lodi founded Agra as a capital, and Ibrahim Lodi's defeat at Panipat opened the way for the Mughals.

extents.label: Approximate extent under Sikandar Lodi (c. 1510 CE)

cities.name: Delhi
cities.note: Capital of Bahlul Lodi.

cities.name: Agra
cities.note: Founded as capital by Sikandar Lodi in 1504.

cities.name: Jaunpur
cities.note: Capital of the rival Sharqi sultans, annexed 1479.

cities.name: Lahore
cities.note: Punjab governorship whose holder invited Babur.

events.title: Bahlul Lodi
events.summary: The Afghan governor of Sirhind takes Delhi and founds the dynasty.

events.title: Jaunpur Sultanate annexed
events.summary: Bahlul ends the Sharqi sultanate after decades of war.

events.title: Agra founded
events.summary: Sikandar Lodi builds a new capital on the Yamuna.

events.title: Ibrahim Lodi

cities.name: Elichpur

events.title: Bijapur and Ahmadnagar break away
events.summary: Bahmani governors found the Adil Shahi and Nizam Shahi dynasties.

events.title: Golconda's Qutb Shahis
events.summary: Sultan Quli establishes the dynasty that rules the Telugu country for 170 years.

events.title: Battle of Talikota

events.title: Charminar

events.title: Chand Bibi defends Ahmadnagar

events.title: Fall of Bijapur

events.title: Siege of Golconda

kingdoms.summary: Europe's first and longest-lasting colonial presence in India, run from Goa as the Estado da Índia; its fortified ports dominated the Arabian Sea spice trade in the 16th century.

cities.name: Hooghly

events.title: Vasco da Gama at Calicut

events.title: Albuquerque takes Goa

events.title: Diu fortified

events.title: Basilica of Bom Jesus

events.title: Bombay given to England
events.summary: The islands pass to Charles II as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry.

events.title: Marathas take Bassein
events.summary: Chimaji Appa's siege ends Portuguese rule in the Northern Province.

events.title: Annexation of Goa
events.summary: Indian forces take Goa, Daman and Diu in 36 hours, ending 451 years of Portuguese rule.

kingdoms.name: Mughal Empire
kingdoms.summary: Founded by Babur after Panipat; under Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb it was one of the largest and richest states in the world, known for the Taj Mahal and a synthesis of Persian and Indian culture.

cities.name: Kabul

cities.name: Aurangabad

cities.name: Dhaka

events.title: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi and founds the empire.

events.title: Second Battle of Panipat
events.summary: The young Akbar's regent Bairam Khan defeats Hemu.

events.title: Fatehpur Sikri built
events.summary: Akbar builds a new capital honouring the Sufi saint Salim Chishti.

events.title: Akbar's religious debates
events.summary: Akbar's Ibadat Khana hosts Hindu, Jain, Christian and Muslim scholars; he promotes 'sulh-i kul', universal peace.

events.title: Taj Mahal begun

events.title: Golconda taken
events.summary: Aurangzeb's conquest of the Deccan sultanates brings the empire to its greatest size.

events.title: Death of Aurangzeb
events.summary: After decades of Deccan wars the emperor dies near Ahmadnagar; decline follows quickly.

events.summary: The Persian ruler carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.

events.title: Rebellion and the end
events.summary: Rebels rally to Bahadur Shah Zafar; the British exile him to Rangoon and abolish the dynasty.

kingdoms.name: Sur Empire
kingdoms.summary: Sher Shah Suri drove Humayun out of India and in five years built an efficient administration — the silver rupiya, a land survey and the Grand Trunk Road with its caravanserais.

events.title: Battle of Kannauj
events.summary: Humayun is defeated again and flees India; Sher Shah takes Delhi.

events.title: The rupiya
events.summary: Sher Shah standardises a silver coin, ancestor of today's rupee.

events.title: Rohtas Fort begun
events.summary: A vast fortress with 12 gates rises on the Grand Trunk Road.

events.title: Grand Trunk Road
events.summary: The ancient highway is rebuilt from Bengal to the Indus with wells, trees and inns.

events.title: Death at Kalinjar

events.summary: Victory at Sirhind restores Mughal rule in Delhi.

events.title: Hemu's last stand
events.summary: The Sur general Hemu briefly takes Delhi as king before his defeat at Panipat.
